Architecture

The service has three layers. Each one only talks to the layer next to it.

Browser
   |  GET /analysis, POST /pull-data, POST /update-analysis
   v
Web layer ........ flask_app.py (+ templates/, static/)
   |                         |
   | Pull Data               | page / Update Analysis
   v                         v
ETL layer ........ pull_data.py -> scrape.py -> clean.py
   |
   v
Database layer ... load_data.py (writes)   models.py + orm_queries.py (reads)
                   db_config.py (DATABASE_URL)          query_data.py (raw SQL)
   |
   v
PostgreSQL: one table, ``applicants``

Web layer

src.flask_app builds the application with src.flask_app.create_app(). The factory receives three functions, so tests can replace any of them with a fake:

  • scraper() returns new Grad Café entries (default: the live pull pipeline);

  • loader(rows) stores them and returns how many were new (default: src.load_data.insert_rows());

  • query() returns the analysis dictionary (default: src.orm_queries.run_analyses()).

A src.flask_app.PullState object holds the busy flag, the last pull’s result and the latest analysis. src.flask_app.format_analysis() turns the analysis into the labelled, formatted answers the page shows.

ETL layer (extract, transform, load)

  • Extract: src.scrape checks robots.txt, fetches pages (urllib3, or Chrome after an HTTP 403), parses each page with BeautifulSoup and finds the next page’s link. src.pull_data.scrape_new() walks the pages from newest to oldest and keeps only entries whose p_id is not in the database yet.

  • Transform: src.clean.clean_data() removes leftover HTML, decodes entities, trims whitespace and drops duplicate entries.

  • Load: src.load_data.insert_rows() converts every value (text, number, date, NULL) and inserts the batch in one transaction.

Database layer

  • One table, applicants, with the 15 required Module 3 columns. p_id (the number at the end of the entry’s URL) is the primary key.

  • src.db_config is the only place that knows where the database is (DATABASE_URL).

  • Writes use psycopg (src.load_data). Reads for the page use SQLAlchemy (src.models, src.orm_queries). src.query_data answers the same questions in raw SQL for the command line.
